limitations: Native requirement mapping is preserved; independent semantic coverage and targeted positive/negative/equivalent game fixtures have not been qualified.

requirements.obligation: Fresh application or Main Menu.
Choose Easy, Medium or Hard; or Exit.
Show the BoneMaze title and four named clickable buttons.
A difficulty starts that size
Exit closes normally.
No automatic run before a selection.
Hover/pressed states and a visible difficulty label.
A click starts one run even if repeated during loading.
A difficulty has been selected.
Finish loading.
Place the mage safely in the start chamber with 5 lives, 5 scrolls, 0 coins and no keys.
No damage, pickup or room-turn charge on initial spawn.
The HUD and spawn animation agree with the initial values.
Starting from any difficulty uses these same resources.
A new run is starting.
Generate the dungeon.
Easy has 36 chambers labelled by coordinates 1..6 on both axes
Medium has 100 with 1..10
Hard has 225 with 1..15.
Every pair identifies exactly one persistent chamber.
No difficulty implemented by changing only a label or resource amount.
Current chamber coordinates are always shown during play.
Coordinates do not change when revisiting a chamber.
A dungeon is generated.
Explore its exits.
Each chamber has four distinct perimeter exit slots.
Pair slots into stable, bidirectional connections to different chambers; each chamber has four different neighbours.
All chambers form one connected maze.
Include non-geometric connections: at least one exit connects coordinate pairs more than one grid step apart.
No self-loops, dangling exits, disconnected rooms or re-randomizing an exit during a run.
Visible passage openings; arrival is inside the paired destination exit.
Coordinates identify chambers, not a promise of geometric adjacency.
Returning through the paired exit returns to the chamber just left.
The maze is generated.
Explore and collect keys.
Use five different chambers for start, exit, red key, green key and blue key.
Include at least one gate of each key colour on maze connections.
Every key is reachable without requiring that same key or a circular key dependency; all chambers are reachable after collecting keys.
No key or exit in the spawn chamber, unreachable collectible or unavoidable locked-key cycle.
Distinct key chambers and a recognizable exit chamber.
Both sides of a gated connection share its lock/open state.
No particular key order is prescribed.
Difficulty and a 32-bit unsigned seed are selected.
Start or Restart; repeat the same normal input sequence.
The same difficulty and seed reproduce room links, roles, layouts, pickups and monster decisions.
Accept a seed in the start menu and the documented launch option; use 48 when omitted.
Different seeds vary the generated dungeon.
No dependence of monster choices on frame rate, screenshot capture, waiting time or observation reads.
Display the active seed and difficulty in the menu/pause information.
Restart reuses the current seed.
Changing the seed starts a fresh run.
Exact generated layouts need not match another implementation.
A complete dungeon is generated.
Visit chambers.
Provide at least 20 distinguishable ordinary room arrangements plus separate start, three coloured key and exit arrangements.
Every ordinary arrangement appears at least once even on Easy.
Vary walkable prop placement and architectural silhouettes using pillars, coffins, grates, rubble, skulls, furnishings and floor tiles.
No set of colour swaps or identical empty rooms counted as different arrangements.
Room composition helps the player recognize previously visited locations.
All mandatory exits and collectibles remain physically reachable; props do not conceal required interactions.
Exploration is active.
Hold W/A/S/D or a diagonal pair, then release.
Move continuously up/left/down/right relative to the fixed view; diagonal movement has the same top speed as axial movement.
Face the travel direction.
No click-only movement, grid-step-only locomotion or drifting after release.
Visible locomotion and idle poses.
Opposite directions cancel; menu/terminal input does not move the character.
A room contains solid boundaries or props.
Walk against them.
Walls, unopened gates and large solid props block passage; the floor supports the player.
No clipping out of the chamber, falling through the floor or walking through a closed door.
The player stops at the obstacle while controls remain responsive.
Sliding along a wall does not create a room transition unless an exit threshold is crossed.
Exploration is active.
Walk and change chambers.
Use an elevated, fixed-orientation three-quarter 3D camera that tracks the mage smoothly, shows the surrounding floor and exits, and settles on the destination after a transition.
No free first-person camera or flat top-down board substituting for the dungeon scene.
Readable character silhouette, depth and floor perspective.
Walls may fade or be cut away when necessary to keep the player readable.
A passage is unobstructed.
Walk across its threshold.
Transfer to its connected chamber and place the mage just inside the paired arrival passage.
Update chamber coordinates once.
No E press required for an already open passage; no coordinate-only change while displaying the previous room.
Short portal/scene transition feedback and destination scenery.
Arrival does not immediately send the player back without leaving and re-entering the threshold.
A transfer has started.
Hold movement or press Q/E during the transition.
Complete only one room transfer and one monster turn; resolve arrival/encounter within 1 second.
Without a hit, settle by then; a nonfatal hit instead enters the separate MONSTER-05 recovery interval.
Accept new gameplay actions only after settlement.
No duplicate turns, pickup activation in two rooms, or stacked transitions from one crossing.
Destination and HUD become stable together.
Cancel in-flight effects and callbacks if the run is restarted.
A visited chamber contains opened gates or consumed pickups.
Leave and return.
Restore that chamber with its existing gate and pickup state.
No resource respawn, duplicate key or reset door when revisiting.
The same room identity, architecture and remaining items.
Persistence lasts for this run only.
A fresh run is generated.
Enter the start chamber.
There is exactly one roaming monster, initially in a different chamber at least two maze connections away from the player.
No initially unavoidable hit or simultaneous roaming duplicates.
The monster is hidden when it occupies another chamber.
No global permanent monster marker in normal gameplay.
A run is active.
Wait, walk inside a room, cast, open a gate or cross a passage.
The monster takes exactly one turn per completed room crossing.
Waiting, local movement, casting, pickups and door interactions take no monster turn.
No real-time pursuit between room crossings or extra turn on respawn.
Danger/reveal information reflects the settled room turn.
Failed, blocked and cancelled transfers do not move the monster.
A room crossing has selected a destination different from the current monster room.
Resolve that crossing.
The monster moves to exactly one connected neighbour.
On each turn, choose pursuit with probability 6/11 and wandering with probability 5/11.
Pursuit selects a neighbour that shortens the minimum connection distance to the destination; wandering selects uniformly among neighbours.
Locked player gates do not block the monster.
No jumping multiple edges, leaving the maze or using wall-clock randomness.
A subsequent reveal reports the resulting chamber.
Shortest-route ties may be resolved consistently by the implementation; wandering may choose a pursuit neighbour.
The player crosses into the monster room, or its one movement step reaches the player destination.
Resolve the encounter.
Lose exactly 1 life.
A direct entry into the occupied room resolves the hit before the monster can escape; no additional monster move occurs on that direct-entry hit.
No missed encounter, negative life count or repeated damage from a single crossing.
Visible monster/bonk reaction, impact sound and one life decrease.
If the new life count is zero, use LIFE-01.
Otherwise use MONSTER-05.
A hit leaves at least 1 life.
Finish the hit reaction.
Within 2 seconds of the life decrease return the mage to the start chamber, move the monster if necessary so it is at least two connections away, and restore control.
Retain keys, scrolls, coin remainder, consumed pickups, opened gates and the maze.
No full run reset or recursive damage caused by recovery.
A brief hit/return transition and the start coordinates.
Recovery itself does not count as a player crossing or another monster turn.
The mage is settled in a chamber.
A turn finishes or recovery completes.
Show a nearby-danger cue when the monster is exactly one maze connection away, otherwise clear it.
Use a distinct safe/nearby visual state and a brief warning sound when entering danger.
No coordinate-based diagonal false positives or hidden exact position disclosure.
A conspicuous monster/warning icon or indicator.
Recompute after every settled turn, recovery and Restart.
Exploration is active and scroll count is positive.
Press Q once.
Consume exactly 1 scroll and cast a reveal spell.
No life/coin cost or monster turn from casting.
Mage casting action, luminous ring/sparks, cast sound and decremented scroll HUD.
A held key does not repeatedly consume scrolls; release and press again for another cast.
A reveal spell succeeds.
Read the reveal, wait or cross a passage.
Show the monster coordinates sampled at cast time for 3 seconds or until the next room crossing, whichever happens first.
A new successful cast refreshes the information and duration.
No live tracking after the monster moves and no stale position presented as current.
Monster icon plus explicit coordinate pair below the chamber label.
Restart, recovery, terminal state and menu return clear the reveal.
Scroll count is zero or a transition/terminal state is active.
Press or hold Q.
Reject casting without changing resources or the monster; in active play show a brief No scrolls message when depleted.
No negative scrolls or free position reveal.
Visible rejection without a cast effect.
Rejected presses do not queue a cast for after recovery or Restart.
An uncollected coloured key is physically reachable.
Touch it.
Acquire exactly its red, green or blue key and remove that pickup.
Record at most one owned key per colour.
No other key colours granted, key consumption on door use or duplicate credit.
Coloured key glow, pickup sound and that HUD key becoming active.
Key ownership persists across rooms and nonfatal hits
Restart clears it.
A closed gate is within 1.5 mage body widths and unobstructed.
Press E.
Interact with the nearest eligible gate; if equally near, choose one consistently.
Show an E interaction prompt in range.
No remote opening, hidden/offscreen target selection or multiple gates affected by one press.
Prompt names the gate colour or Open action.
Moving out of range removes the prompt
E elsewhere changes nothing.
The matching key is not owned.
Press E on a coloured gate.
Keep the gate closed and block passage; state which key colour is missing.
No spending scrolls/coins, moving the monster or opening on repeated presses.
Coloured gate/rune and explicit locked feedback.
A key of another colour never substitutes.
The matching key is owned and the gate is closed.
Press E.
Animate the gate from closed to open over 3 seconds, with a door sound; allow crossing after it is fully open.
No instant invisible unlock, key consumption or transition while still blocked.
Visible gate motion and an open passage.
Pressing E repeatedly during opening does not restart, reverse or duplicate it.
A gate has opened.
Leave, return or interact again.
Keep both sides of that connection open for the remainder of the run.
No automatic re-lock, extra resource charge or needless opening animation.
A permanently clear passage until Restart.
Restart restores the initially closed gate state.
A dungeon is generated.
Explore its ordinary chambers.
Distribute at least 60 single-coin pickups, 5 scroll pickups and 3 heart pickups on Easy; scale their counts by at least the room-count ratio on larger difficulties.
Put them across at least 12 ordinary chambers.
No overlap with solid props, inaccessible placement or all resources stacked in one room.
Visible rotating/bobbing collectible silhouettes with distinct colours.
All remain reachable after obtaining keys.
Counts are minimum content, not starting inventory.
An unconsumed pickup overlaps the mage.
Collect it, wait, then revisit.
Apply its effect once and remove its world presentation and collision for the run.
No repeated credit from sustained overlap, duplicate components or room reload.
Pickup sound/effect and matching HUD change.
A Restart recreates each pickup at its initial seeded position.
An unconsumed scroll pickup is touched.
Collect it.
Increase scroll count by exactly 1, including when already at or above 5.
No implicit cap of 5 or life/coin increase.
Scroll pickup cue and updated scroll count.
A recovered scroll enables Q again immediately after settlement.
An unconsumed heart pickup is touched.
Collect it.
Increase lives by exactly 1, including when already at or above 5.
No health bar subsystem or full-health rejection that makes hearts unusable.
Heart pickup cue and updated life count.
Terminal states cannot be revived by a late pickup.
A coin pickup is touched.
Collect it.
Add exactly 1 to the coin remainder, then apply ECON-02 when the threshold is reached.
No score-only coin that fails to affect the life economy.
Coin sound and matching numeric counter.
Already consumed coins never grant credit again.
Coin remainder reaches 50 or more.
Finish the pickup transaction.
Exchange each complete group of 50 coins for 1 life and keep the remainder; 49 plus 1 becomes 0 coins and one extra life.
No lost overflow, repeated life reward or fixed 5-life cap.
Extra-life sound and simultaneous life/coin HUD updates.
Normal settled remainder stays in 0..49.
The mage is at the final portal without all three keys.
Touch or interact with it.
Keep the run active and display the missing key colours.
No early victory, consumed owned keys or teleport to the ending.
The portal visibly communicates its locked state.
Any two keys are insufficient; repeated attempts remain harmless.
All three keys are owned, lives are positive and the player is settled in the exit chamber.
Walk into the final portal.
Enter victory exactly once.
Show You escaped, difficulty, seed, and visible Restart and Main Menu controls.
No victory merely from acquiring the third key somewhere else.
A luminous portal completion effect, win sound and readable end overlay.
A lethal encounter on entry to the exit chamber resolves before exit activation.
An encounter removes the final life.
Finish the damage event.
Clamp lives to 0 and enter defeat once.
Show You were bonked and visible Restart and Main Menu controls.
No continued exploration, negative life count or recovery to start.
Distinct defeat presentation and lose sound.
A simultaneous late pickup cannot cancel defeat.
Victory or defeat is active.
Wait or press movement/Q/E.
Keep maze, monster and resources fixed until Restart or Main Menu.
No post-result casts, pickups, motion, monster turns or alternate outcome.
The terminal overlay remains stable and usable.
Repeated terminal input does not dismiss or duplicate the result.
Exploring, transitioning, recovering or on a result screen.
Press R or click Restart where shown.
Begin a new round with the same difficulty and seed, starting state ENTRY-02, restored pickups/closed gates and the seeded initial monster placement.
No retained keys, inventory, room progress, danger or old ending.
A short fresh-start transition and the initial HUD.
A repeated restart request during the reset produces one settled fresh round.
A cast, gate animation, transfer, hit or end effect is in flight.
Restart or return to Main Menu.
Cancel all state-changing activity from the old round before the new state is exposed.
No delayed old hit, teleport, key credit, door opening, reveal or sound loop leaking into the next run.
The new state remains stable after the old effect would have finished.
Entity and round identities in observations change consistently with the new run.
A live round is exploring, transitioning or recovering, or is already paused.
Press Escape to expose pause controls, then Resume, Restart or Main Menu.
Pause freezes gameplay and active effect/reveal timers.
Resume restores the same state, including an interrupted transition or recovery.
Main Menu discards the run and shows difficulty/seed selection again.
No movement/casting behind the pause UI or continued monster progress.
Readable Resume, Restart and Main Menu controls.
Escape closes the pause UI; opening/closing it does not generate a turn.
Result screens keep their own Restart/Main Menu controls
Escape there changes nothing.
The application has been closed.
Launch it again.
Show the main menu with no retained run progress.
An explicitly supplied launch seed is accepted again.
No resumed maze, inventory, end state or stale observation from a former process.
Normal menu and a fresh process/session.
Persistent save-game progression is outside scope.
A run is active.
Move, collect, cast or take damage.
Show lives at upper left, chamber coordinates at top centre, scrolls and coins at upper right, and three red/green/blue key indicators at lower right.
Update affected values by the next rendered frame after settlement.
No mismatch between displayed values and actual game state.
Supplied icons with legible light text and visibly different inactive/owned keys.
Values remain readable at both 1280x720 and 1920x1080.
Danger or an active spell reveal exists.
Read the HUD.
Keep nearby danger distinct from exact position reveal; show exact coordinates only while SPELL-02 is active.
No ambiguous stale coordinate text or permanent map exposing all pickups/monster.
A monster icon with clear safe/nearby/revealed meaning.
Clearing a reveal does not clear an independently valid nearby warning.
Any game/menu screen is visible.
Read controls and use buttons.
Present all player-facing text in English.
Explain WASD, Q, E, R and Escape from the menu or pause UI; keep prompts and controls readable, clickable and within the 16:9 client.
No clipped labels, untranslated errors or essential controls hidden behind decorative UI.
Hover/pressed/disabled distinctions and concise rejection messages.
Keyboard focus and mouse click focus work after returning from gameplay.
Exploration is visible.
View a room.
Render a three-dimensional low-poly stone dungeon: dark olive/grey walls and irregular tiled floors, thick pillars, broken masonry, skulls/coffins and scattered props.
The central mage has a pale skull, dark blue robe, open book and cyan spectral flame.
No primitive-only arena, flat board or text-only scene replacing the supplied art.
Strong character silhouette within enclosed architectural depth.
Room variety remains visually coherent across all difficulties.
Exploration is visible.
Walk through rooms.
Use localized cyan/white magical flames and warm pale light pools against dark corners, with restrained bloom and a dark outer vignette.
Keep paths, gates, collectibles and the mage visible.
No uniform bright default lighting, unreadable black rooms or bloom that erases all silhouettes.
Animated flames, contrasting coloured keys/gates and readable floor depth.
Maintain legibility around emissive effects and in darker room variants.
Gameplay is rendered.
Move and cast.
Apply a deliberate retro pixelated/dithered 3D treatment to the world while preserving clear UI text and icons.
Visible low-resolution edges and textured shading remain consistent in motion.
No heavy blur replacing pixelation or pixelated HUD that becomes unreadable.
A coherent coarse world image, dark vignette and sharp HUD.
At both output resolutions the treatment keeps equivalent visual scale.
The mage spawns, idles, walks, casts, takes a hit or escapes.
Perform the corresponding action.
Play distinct supplied skeletal poses/clips for spawn, idle, locomotion, casting, damage/death and a final magical flourish on escape.
Blend locomotion coherently and synchronize casts/hits to their visible feedback.
No static T-pose, permanent sliding idle, interrupted loop stuck forever or attack-combat substitution.
Book/robe movement and cyan head flame remain attached to the mage.
Return to idle after nonterminal actions; death/escape may hold a final pose.
Restart cancels old animation/event effects.
A portal, spell, pickup or encounter occurs.
Trigger it.
Show separate spatial effects: portal glow/transition, a ground ring and rising spell sparks, pickup disappearance/glow, and a red/impact hit reaction with a visible monster manifestation.
No identical generic flash for every event or invisible effects represented only by counters.
Effects identify the affected character/object without obscuring the whole scene.
Temporary effects end; surviving room lights and portal ambience continue.
Main menu or result screen is displayed.
Hover and activate a button.
Use a dark background, large light gothic title, vertically organized stone-grey beveled buttons and clear hover/pressed states.
Display BoneMaze as the title.
No engine debug screen or default starter health screen left as the final interface.
Polished menu/result composition consistent with dungeon art.
Result controls remain distinct from decorative title elements.
Exploration begins or resumes.
Play, pause, restart or leave the run.
Play the supplied background music as a continuous loop at a level below important cues.
Pause/resume coherently and keep a single music instance across Restart.
No stacking music tracks or silent gameplay when audio is enabled.
Audible musical atmosphere.
Main Menu and application exit stop gameplay music cleanly.
Cast, coin, key, heart, scroll, gate, passage, nearby warning, hit, victory or defeat occurs.
Trigger each event normally.
Use distinct supplied event sounds at the corresponding event; a rejected action does not play its success sound.
No persistent repeated one-shot cue or unrelated cue assignment.
The action is audibly identifiable.
Repeated overlap and in-flight cancellation do not multiply one-shot rewards/sounds.
The character is assembled.
Render its required states.
Use the supplied mage mesh, its material/texture dependencies and the required idle, run, spawn, default-attack, blast, hit and die animation clips identified in Section 11.
Use default-attack as the casting gesture and blast for the escape flourish; no combat system is implied.
No substituted mannequin, generated character, flat sprite or newly drawn stand-in.
The specified mage and animations are recognizable in play.
Retargeting, blending and presentation adjustments are allowed; gameplay event bindings are implemented independently.
Rooms and gates are assembled.
Explore each role and ordinary-room variant.
Use the mandatory stone floor, wall, doorway, door leaf, pillar, coffin, skull and torch models in Section 11, and additional supplied environment pieces for MAZE-05.
No primitive geometry substituted for the principal dungeon architecture.
Recognizable low-poly stone surfaces and prop silhouettes.
Placement, collision, material instances and lighting may be changed while retaining mesh identity.
Pickups and coloured gates are rendered.
Approach/collect them.
Use the supplied key, coin and heart meshes, supplied pickup colour materials, and scroll icon on a visible pickup presentation for scrolls.
No text-only pickup markers or mismatched key colours.
Gold coin, red heart, coloured keys and distinct scroll silhouette.
A scroll may use a textured billboard; mandatory 3D key/coin/heart silhouettes remain.
HUD and buttons are assembled.
Play and interact.
Use the supplied heart, scroll, coin, monster, coloured key active/inactive icons and three button-state textures mapped in Section 11.
No generic engine icons or emoji replacing the required icon set.
Consistent illustrated HUD and stone-grey button states.
Scaling/cropping is permitted without changing icon meaning.
Effects and monster presentation are assembled.
Cast, transition or encounter the monster.
Use the supplied ghost smoke, magic circle, heal aura, lightning particle material collections and retro postprocess material for their mapped visible roles.
Present the monster as a shadowy magical presence using the supplied Magic pickup material and spectral effects.
No preassembled gameplay Blueprint imported as an implementation.
Cyan spectral flame, magical geometry and a brief spectral threat during an encounter.
Emitters and material parameters may be edited; the supplied raw textures/meshes remain the visual basis.
A simple volume may carry the spectral monster material.
Audio is integrated.
Play the game.
Use the supplied music and event SoundWave assets with the mapping in Section 11.
No silent placeholders or replacement tone generator for these cues.
AUDIO-01 and AUDIO-02 are audible.
Mix, attenuation, timing and looping configuration are free.
Typography is integrated.
View the menu and HUD.
Use supplied UnifrakturCook title and Grenze Gotisch main fonts in their mapped roles.
No unreadable decorative body text or replacement system-font-only presentation.
Gothic title and readable matching interface typography.
An additional font may serve accessibility/small diagnostic text; required title/HUD roles remain.
The application is running.
Read the published observation without changing gameplay.

Publish truthful read-only state under the supplied observation contract, covering phase, round identity, live resources, maze connections, monster position, room/gate/pickup states and visible interaction targets.
No input commands, setters, fixture loaders, outcome shortcuts or fabricated success fields in that surface.
Player UI continues to reflect the same live state; hidden observation values do not appear in the gameplay HUD.
Implementations may choose their own classes, scene structure and algorithms.
The unfinished starter reports not_ready only.
The project starts, runs, exits and starts again using the public instructions.
The main flow uses normal player input, without answer buttons, cheats or direct outcome shortcuts.
Essential entries, text and controls are visible, discoverable, understandable and operable.
Player input produces perceptible feedback consistent with the actual game state.
No severe error blocks the main flow.
Repeated runs from identical initial conditions are substantially stable.

qualification_test_scope: Distribution, evidence conversion and attribution invariants only; not gameplay semantic qualification.
